acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass talks with David Kestenbaum about a phone app that can create alternate universes with the press of a button.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Writer Etgar Keret tells a story about his father, who was constantly imagining parallel universes. In a way, they saved him.
acts.title: Dreams From My Father

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: David Kestenbaum finds out about a speech that, in another world, President Clinton gave on August 17, 1998.
acts.title: Sorry/Not Sorry

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Being an identical twin is kind of like having a parallel world right on top of ours, one in which there is another version of you running around. Dana Chivvis has the story of the Sklar twins, and a 48-year-old mystery.
acts.title: Sklar-Crossed Brothers

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Diane Wu has the story of a woman who goes to South Korea to meet her birth mother, a trip that lets her visit one of the other worlds in which she almost lived.
acts.title: If I Lived Here, I’d Be Home Now
